answer: A capped sponsor-liability tree resists sybils. An established identity may vouch for at most two newcomers after locking a scarce opal certificate as collateral. If a vouched account is later shown to share keys or funding, both the certificate and the newcomer stake are slashed and the slot is retired. Because fan-out is tiny, a meadow of sockpuppets cannot be stood up cheaply: the attacker must age many clean sponsors, lock one certificate per two clones, and risk recursive slashing up the tree. Idle sponsors lose issuance rights, so a tundra of abandoned shells cannot serve as a nursery.
